subject: Approval request: automated fallback & sticky-version carveout for CardioTech ramp
messages:
From: lauren_bishop
To: marissa_cole, marcus_lin, priyom_das
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Approval request: automated fallback & sticky-version carveout for CardioTech ramp

Team —

CardioTech is looking to kick off a large traffic ramp next Monday (week-of 3/20). Their ramp plan will shift ~55% of production reads to the new inference variant over ~48 hours. Legal and procurement have signed, but they insisted we enable the fastest possible recovery path in case of regressions. They want two things that deviate from our default rollout guardrails:

1) Automatic fallback to the old model variant (no manual approval) at the service-layer if 5m P95 latency degrades >40% OR error rate spikes >2% absolute.
2) Temporary sticky-version (pin) for 2 hours after any fallback event so we avoid oscillation during re-evaluation.

Why this matters: CardioTech is a tier-1 prospect and this ramp ties directly to our committed SLA language and an onboarding milestone in the deal. They will place sensitive traffic (PHI-adjacent) behind our Dedicated pool. We can manage risk, but operations needs an explicit carveout to enable both auto-fallback and the sticky-version behaviour for this customer only.

Ask: formal approval from Marcus (SRE lead) and Priyom (Platform) to enable the carveout for CardioTech for the duration of their ramp window (3/20 00:00 UTC — 3/22 23:59 UTC). I attached the proposed policy and telemetry thresholds. If approved, I’ll notify CardioTech and schedule an on-call alignment call.

Quick risk mitigation notes (from sales perspective):
- We guarantee a canary window and will run a shadow run for 24 hours before traffic shift.
- If the fallback triggers, we will open a postmortem with CardioTech within 24 hours.
- Procurement has agreed to include a mutual action item for a re-test before re-roll.

Thanks —
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai

Attachments: cardiotech_canary_policy_v2.pdf, ramp_telemetry_thresholds.csv

From: marcus_lin
To: lauren_bishop, marissa_cole, priyom_das
Cc: ops-oncall@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Approval request: automated fallback & sticky-version carveout for CardioTech ramp

Lauren —

Thanks for the summary and the attachments. I reviewed the thresholds: auto-fallback on 5m P95 +40% or error rate +2% is aggressive but reasonable for a single-account carveout provided we hard-limit the scope to that Dedicated pool and maintain human-in-the-loop visibility. Two comments from SRE:

- Telemetry gating: we need both a primary trigger (latency/error) and a secondary confirmation window (two consecutive 1-minute samples) to avoid false positives from transient spikes.
- Sticky-duration: 2 hours is likely fine, but we should add an autorevert condition if the downstream health metrics improve for a sustained 30m window to minimize customer impact.

Operational steps I need before approval:
1) A short runbook for the on-call team describing the fallback detection signal, expected actions, and escalation tree.
2) A tagging mechanism so metrics and logs from this carveout are labeled "cardiotech_ramp_v2" in our observability stack.
3) Confirmation that the change can be toggled remotely per-customer without redeploying runtime.

If Priyom signs off on the implementation constraints above, I’ll approve the carveout for the 72-hour window.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

From: priyom_das
To: lauren_bishop, marcus_lin, marissa_cole
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Approval request: automated fallback & sticky-version carveout for CardioTech ramp

Team —

I’m fine enabling this as a temporary exception under these constraints:
- Implementation will be via our per-tenant routing policy; no runtime changes required. Toggle will be a config flip in the control plane (audit logged).
- We will implement Marcus’s secondary confirmation (two consecutive 1-minute windows) and a 30-minute sustain window for autorevert.
- We’ll label telemetry with "cardiotech_ramp_v2" and create a dedicated dashboard.
- Ops runbook will be in Confluence by EOD today and I’ll add a short PagerDuty escalation path with a separate routing key.

I approve the carveout conditionally. Lauren, please ensure CardioTech agrees to the observability terms and the 24-hour shadow run before we flip traffic. Also, remind them that any post-fallback re-roll requires a coordinated smoke test.

Priyom
Priyom Das
Director, Serving Platform
priyom.das@redwood.ai

From: Samantha Cho <samantha.cho@cardiotech.com>
To: lauren_bishop, marissa_cole
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 14:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Approval request: automated fallback & sticky-version carveout for CardioTech ramp

Lauren / Marissa —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. CardioTech accepts the proposed carveout with the operational constraints Marcus and Priyom outlined. We are scheduling the 24-hour shadow run to start 3/19 00:00 UTC and the main ramp to begin 3/20 00:00 UTC. A few items for the record:

- CardioTech requests a read-only dashboard link for the ramp telemetry and an alert subscription to the fallback trigger.
- We expect a joint postmortem and a remediation timeline if fallback occurs.
- We will not re-route production traffic back to our previous variant without a coordinated smoke test.

Please send the on-call calendar invite and the Confluence runbook link when ready.

Best,
Samantha Cho
Head of Platform, CardioTech
Samantha.cho@cardiotech.com
